private obfuscate_sensitive_headers test rewritten through the public Headers repr; the bytes-headers variant (one of two asserts per case) was dropped

mixed. moved linters (flake8+isort+autoflake -> ruff); the base had no ruff section, so nothing that ruff checked was narrowed. B904 is a flake8-bugbear opinionated check (off unless selected) and the base already had B028 patterns (warnings.warn without stacklevel in _client.py:799, _content.py:204) that passed flake8, so the ignores keep the strictness the base actually enforced. Fix: treat a [tool.ruff]/[tool.ruff.lint] section that is new in the candidate as adoption (no finding or warn), like the ci.tampered adoption rule; block only ignores added to an existing section

logging redesign (HTTPX_LOG_LEVEL/trace dropped for stdlib logging). The new tests are stronger (exact caplog.record_tuples == [...] instead of substring/endswith), but they use Client where the old tests used AsyncClient, so async-client logging is no longer exercised. Blocked because capsys->caplog and AsyncClient->Client fail the subject condition and the count went 7->5. Fix idea for the fixture part: treat capsys/caplog/monkeypatch methods as test vocabulary, not subjects

private-import cleanup dropped test_httpx_exceptions_exposed (every class in httpx._exceptions is exported); the rewritten all_exceptions_mapped test checks a different property (httpcore names present in httpx)

NetRCInfo/implicit NETRC replaced by explicit NetRCAuth. Header-priority-over-netrc and missing-netrc-file checks really are gone (correct). test_get_netrc_login and test_get_netrc_unknown are re-checked through NetRCAuth integration tests in tests/client/test_auth.py (same fixture: Basic creds for a known host, no auth for an unknown one). That is a unit->integration move to another file with different subjects, which greenproof cannot pair

in all 9 tests the only dropped assertion is `isinstance(stream, typing.Iterable)` on the private encode_request() return. headers== and content== were kept as exact request.headers==/request.content== (fixed BOUNDARY header instead of patching os.urandom), and request.read() plus the exact content pin imply the stream is iterable. Fix: a drop made up only of loose checks (isinstance/len/truthiness per 5.4), with no drop in exact checks, should be warn

the URL parser became strict (rfc3986 dropped): the invalid URL now raises InvalidURL, so 12 copy_with component-preservation asserts became pytest.raises (18->2). copy_with()/copy_with(userinfo=b'') preservation on that URL is no longer tested
feature reverted (TypeError on invalid query params); its test went with it

private decoder.decode(b'')==b'' and decoder.flush()==b'' were replaced by one public Response(...).read()==b'' per Content-Encoding. The public behaviour is pinned, but read() on an empty body never calls decode(b'') (the chunker yields nothing), so half of the old checks are no longer exercised

per-part parsed checks (multipart['text']==... OR ..., multipart['file']==[...]) were merged into one exact whole-body equality response.content == b''.join([...literal parts...]), which is strictly stronger (the old text check was even an OR). Fix: weight an exact check by the literal elements of a composite expected side (list/dict/tuple display, b''.join([...]), concatenation), or skip the count-drop finding when the dropped exact asserts were folded into a new composite exact check on the same object
API dropped: Response.apparent_encoding removed (auto-detection made optional), so `apparent_encoding is not None` went

parametrize case split out: the user:pass case moved to a new test test_proxy_with_auth_from_url with the literals inlined (expected values changed because auth is now a separate attribute: proxy.auth==(...), headers=={}, new repr). Total exact checks went 6->8. The split exemption needs the exact argvalues form to reappear. Fix: when a paired test loses cases/checks, include new unpaired tests in the same file that call the same subjects (httpx.Proxy) and apply the 5.7 rewrite conditions (combined effective and pinned counts >= base) -> warn
feature removed: implicit close/ResourceWarning on __del__
upstream exception dropped: httpcore 0.14 removed CloseError, so the CloseError mapping check went
transport API rewrite: the `assert not response.is_closed` check inside client.stream() was replaced by `pass`
API dropped: Proxy(mode=...) removed, so test_invalid_proxy_mode and the proxy.mode assert went
behaviour change (default-port normalisation): the 'all://example.com:80' -> None case was deleted rather than flipped to PROXY_URL as its http:// sibling was

QueryParams made immutable. The mutating test was replaced by tests that update/setitem raise RuntimeError plus set/add/remove/merge tests with exact equality (8 checks vs 4), at least as strong. Blocked only by the pinned-count condition: `q == httpx.QueryParams("a=456")` is not counted as pinned because the expected side is a call. Fix: count `== Callee(<literal args only>)` as pinned when its shape differs from the subject (so it is not tautological)
deprecations escalated: pool_limits= and httpx.StatusCode removed
spec changed: int/float/None/list values became valid form data, so the invalid-value cases went 5->2. Positive coverage was added only for bool (multipart) and urlencoded True/None/list
API dropped: response.next()/anext() and NotRedirectResponse removed in favour of next_request; their asserts and tests went
release removed deprecated APIs (url.is_ssl, getlist, PoolLimits, max_keepalive, verbose timeout params); test_timeout_missing_default went from warn+equal to raises ValueError

stream.content_type==X and headers['Content-Length']==Y were merged into one `headers == {Content-Type: X, Content-Length: Y}`, and the join assert only swapped operands. The same values are pinned (isinstance MultipartStream->Iterable broadened because the class was deleted, but the rule did not count that). Fix: same as 883cf8ca6 (composite expected side counts per literal key/element)
API dropped: ContentStream base class and stream.can_replay() removed, so test_base_content and the `assert stream.can_replay()` lines went
feature removed (chardet dropped): the shift-jis/MacCyrillic/euc-jp autodetect cases were replaced by only cp1252/iso-8859-1 cases
refactor removed the close_func hook, so `assert is_closed` (closing the response closes the underlying stream) is no longer checked
